name: Havoc
quote: Listen, the sound of metal breaking apart.

voices.label: Good Morning
voices.text: Ah... Professor... you're up early. Me? Yeah, now that I've said good morning, lend me your bed for a second snooze. The early worm gets eaten by the bird, you know. For my personal safety, I've decided to sleep until noon... Zzz... zzz...

voices.label: Good Afternoon
voices.text: ...No good... I've got zero energy. The afternoon sun's so harsh... Haah... I don't feel like working at all. Let's wait a bit more. It won't be too late to start after sundown. "Sharpening the axe doesn't delay the woodcutting." A well-read Professor like you must've heard that one, right?

voices.label: Good Evening
voices.text: It's already evening. If I start working now, that's overtime pay, Professor. Can't be helped, I'm pretty worried about the Oasis construction. If it falls behind schedule and the new cable materials don't pass testing in time, Kuro's streaming rig, Croque's anime projector and Antonina's retro game console will all go on strike. Can't just turn a blind eye to that kind of tragedy~ Alright, let's get to work.

voices.label: Good Night
voices.text: Professor... why are you still working... As a materials science expert, I have to warn you: toughness, hardness, melting point... every material has its limits. You get what I'm saying, right? Then... you can also understand my "occasional" absences, "intermittent" lateness and "every-now-and-then" early leaves, right?

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 1
voices.text: I'm not lazy, I'm energy-efficient. These days, anything with high energy costs and low returns should've been phased out long ago. Me? I've made a huge contribution to saving the Oasis's operands. Professor, how about giving me a public commendation?

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 2
voices.text: Zzz... snore... zzz... Hm?! P-Professor, I-I'm not slacking off! I'm just running a destructive test on this steel cable... Huh? Wait, why's it tangled? I can't... get free... P-Professor! Help me, quick!

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 3
voices.text: Geez, Professor, if you're gonna slack off and nap, why didn't you invite me... Ehehe... Your body's so warm, Professor... Lots of people would be jealous of me sleeping here... prob... ably... Snore... zzz...

voices.label: Home Screen 4
voices.text: People say the Guardians are all problem children: there's a patient, a speed demon, a pervy mad dog, a nagging mom... and I'm the only normal one... A slacking maniac?! What's abnormal about slacking off?! Long live slacking, slacking is the best!!!

voices.label: Home Screen 5
voices.text: Weather this nice calls for a lazy nap. Hm? You say it's cloudy today? Even better. Who'd be in the mood to work on a cloudy day?

voices.label: Interactive Voice 1
voices.text: Hm?! ...You scared me. Oh, it's just you.

voices.label: Interactive Voice 2
voices.text: Hm? Interested in the materials here? Feel free to touch some more~

voices.label: Interactive Voice 3
voices.text: Snore... snore... zzz... Professor... so squishy... looks tasty... zzz...

voices.label: On Duty
voices.text: Fine... But this is the only time I'm working overtime.

voices.label: Obtain
voices.text: Yawn... I'm Havoc. I heard the work atmosphere at the Oasis is relaxed, perfect for slack— I mean, perfect for talent like me. Nice to meet you, Professor.

voices.label: Potential Breakthrough
voices.text: Sharpening the axe never delays the work~

voices.label: Neural Expansion
voices.text: A proper rest is good for body and mind.

voices.label: Max Rank
voices.text: Guess it's time to get serious.

voices.label: Join Team
voices.text: Mm... Time to clock in?

voices.label: Battle Start
voices.text: Geez, you don't give me any time to slack off.

voices.label: Ultimate Skill
voices.text: Single-point breakthrough, pierce through!

voices.label: MVP 1
voices.text: No matter what stands in my way, I'll pierce right through it.

voices.label: MVP 2
voices.text: Clocking out, clocking out!

voices.label: Defeat
voices.text: I'm gonna... take a little nap first...

voices.label: Oath
voices.text:
An oath imprint?! Ah... If I make an oath with you, Professor, could I slack off openly and leave all the work to you? Hehehe... Eh, eh, ehhh! Wait, wait! Professor, come back, I was kidding!
Phew... That scared me. I never thought I'd feel like giving everything I've got for someone. Geez, guess slacker Havoc has to officially clock out. Since you chose me, let me fulfill my duty as your oathbound. From now on, Havoc is running at full power!

voices.label: New Year
voices.text:
Happy New Year, Professor. Hm? I'm in a good mood? Of course! New year, new vibes, everything renewed! Whatever happened last year gets reset when the new year comes. Like my lateness record, and my annual leave! Huh... Because I was late too often last year, my leave this year is cut in half?!
Protest! I protest! This violates labor laws! Protest!

voices.label: Valentine's Day
voices.text: Huh, today's Valentine's Day? Ohh... No wonder the Heartfelt House of Cocoa was running a new-product event. I bought a little on the way, so let's share, Professor. Where's the chocolate? Oh, it's this whole sack behind me. You've gotta replenish sugar after high-intensity work. Eating a bit extra is totally reasonable.

voices.label: Tanabata
voices.text: They say the Cowherd and the Weaver Girl are tied together by a red string, so their longing reaches each other even across the Milky Way. But a red string's so thin, one little snip and it breaks. Isn't that too fragile? If it were me, I'd tie you up good and tight with a steel cable, Professor. With a material that sturdy, neither of us could get away. Well? Wanna try it right now?

voices.label: Halloween
voices.text: Yawn... Happy Halloween, Professor. Not bad, this vampire projection, right? They say vampires sleep soundly all day and only come out at night. Who knew they'd match my schedule so perfectly? Truly a legendary treasure of human mythology... Alright, enough chitchat. Time to recharge. If you can, wake me up in the evening. I'm usually super punctual, you know... Zzz... zzz...

voices.label: Christmas
voices.text:
Christmas is for curling up by the fireplace and turning into a blanket monster. Ahh... So comfy. Professor, I don't think I can move today. Why don't you curl up in the blanket and rest with me?
Huh? We have to go deliver presents to everyone? Haah, can't be helped... Then I'll help you finish fast, and we'll hurry back here to keep being blanket monsters!

voices.label: Birthday Wish
voices.text:
Congrats, Professor, another year older. It's your birthday today, so I gave up my second snooze to come wish you a happy birthday. That shows how important you are to me, right? So listen up. I hope your new year is carefree and happy every day.
Oh right, I almost forgot, I got you a birthday present too... Ta-da! Look, look, it's a fluffy "Coo-Coo Pigeon" blanket cape! Hurry and put it on, and let's slack off together as blanket monsters.

voices.label: Neural Cloud
voices.text: Neural Cloud

voices.label: Intimacy 1
voices.text: Professor, I don't wanna go to work today... I've come down with... Seasonal Laziness Syndrome... also known as the May Blues... Huh? The May Blues aren't a real illness?! Seriously, I thought I'd found the perfect excuse to skip work... Come to think of it, the name doesn't even make sense! Nobody wants to work any day of the year, so why does only lazing around in May get a name? If you ask me, every month of the year should have "don't-wanna-work days," twenty or more per month. The remaining workdays have to guarantee eight-hour shifts and two days off a week. That's the only way to maximize a unit's physical and mental health and relieve both the physical and mental fatigue that work causes. Pretty good proposal, right, Professor?

voices.label: Intimacy 2
voices.text: Hey Professor, did you know? My body's a little different from everyone else's. I'm a materials science expert, after all. In the real world I tested hundreds, thousands of materials to verify data like hardness, flexibility and durability. After I got uploaded to the Cloud, all that data got reflected in my mind too. So my body now is not only durable, it's comfy as well. Wanna give it a squeeze, Professor~? Well? The synthetic skin on my arm is super soft, right? Huh? Wait, Professor, where are you touching? Hey... S-stop... Ahahahahahahahahahaha, st-stop, stop it already... Tickling is cheating, ahahahahahahaha...

voices.label: Intimacy 3
voices.text: You're spacing out, Professor. Something on your mind? Hmm... Honestly, when things get tough, sleeping is the only good solution I know. Sleep it off and you'll forget all your troubles and feel way more relaxed. That's not running away. It's just a buffer before you pick yourself back up. Life goes on, after all... Ah, all that talking wore me out. Anyway, why were you spacing out, Professor? Huh?! The coffee was just so sweet you zoned out for a sec? That's it?!!

voices.label: Intimacy 4
voices.text: P-Professor?! I wasn't spacing out, okay? Seeing this work scene just reminded me of the past. Ahem. I used to have a colleague I worked with. She worked tirelessly, nonstop, until one day she got scrapped in an accident during a destructive test... And the lesson here is: if you work, you die! To live well for both of us, every day I summon my courage, go against my conscience, and slack off with all my might. You understand how hard I'm trying, right, Professor? Phew, all this talking wore me out... I've already worked for 30 minutes! So now it's slacking time~ Professor, for the sake of our physical and mental health, let's ditch work together!

voices.label: Intimacy 5
voices.text: Waaah! P-Professor, why'd you show up all of a sudden?! Did you... see? What's under my clothes... Haah... I didn't really want you to see that. I'm a destructiveness tester. I verify the limits of materials by breaking things... But at the same time, I'm also the best platform for mounting materials. In a way, I'm another... Lind, just one who isn't as sensitive to pain. Every so often they'd take my body apart and fit it with all kinds of weird materials, and send me into extreme environments for testing more times than I can count... Passing out again and again, getting rebuilt again and again. Honestly, I don't really remember what my body originally looked like anymore... Ah, but isn't that kinda cool? Like the legendary Frankenstein~

career:
The SI-DT series is a Doll line designed by Svarog Heavy Industries specifically for destructive testing. Given the damage inevitable in such testing, SI-DT units were designed to be cheap, structurally simple and easy to repair with replaceable parts, ensuring the safety of core components and continued data collection even under severe damage. Once deployed, the SI-DT not only effectively reduced the cost and risk of destructive testing but also improved data collection efficiency, making outstanding contributions to materials science and Doll technology.

However, long-term high-intensity testing kept the SI-DT's attrition rate high. As cheaper alternatives appeared, the SI-DT quickly faded from the market. On Svarog's recommendation, "Havoc," the only remaining intact late-model SI-DT, was sent to 42Lab to take part in the Neural Cloud project.
infoStories:
When applying materials science in practice, metrics such as material lifespan, structure and strength are crucial. Humanity has constantly pursued materials that are stronger, lighter and more ingeniously structured, using them to build ever more advanced things that change the world. Testing a material's strength and structure through destructive experiments is an indispensable part of materials research, though it usually brings collateral damage and sunk costs, and in some cases threatens the physical and mental health of the people running the tests. For these reasons, many research institutions and companies began developing ways to cut testing costs and reduce risk, and Svarog Heavy Industries' answer was the SI-DT series of Dolls.

"Using Dolls to perform high-risk work in place of humans" has always been Svarog's guiding principle in Doll development. Though the principle has drawn growing controversy, there's no denying that it works. The SI-DT not only took over tedious, repetitive destructive work from humans but also served as a platform for destructive materials testing. SI-DT bodies were designed to be simple, easily replaceable and low-cost, yet as strong as possible; they can be repaired quickly even after severe damage, and in extreme cases are even compatible with parts from older Dolls. Most of the SI-DT's cost went into reinforcing data-core protection and the feedback system, which makes the design of its sensory system rather unusual among Dolls. Thanks to these designs, the SI-DT could record the changes in every material across its body more directly and determine their limits.

Where exactly does the name "Havoc" come from? Even she can only shake her head and say she doesn't know, or reply, "Just made it up." Yet the literal meaning is easy enough to grasp—"destruction, chaos"—exactly what she did with all sorts of equipment in test after test.

There's also an unconfirmed theory, absurd but rather amusing: that the name "Havoc" comes from the protagonist of a shooter game released around the millennium, a tall, muscular, free-spirited ace special forces soldier. Perhaps because SI-DT units are generally tall, Havoc got this name. Whatever the reason, Havoc seems quite pleased with it.

As a late-model unit, Havoc joined a research institute under Svarog Heavy Industries at the end of 2056, mainly handling materials testing and data collection. Havoc and the other SI-DT Dolls reportedly took part in research on Doll body materials, contributing to breakthroughs in Doll materials science. However, whenever the topic of her work history comes up, whether she raises it or someone else does, Havoc isn't very keen to talk about it.

"Getting broken over and over still hurts and is a huge pain, y'know? Not as awful as Lind had it... but I swear, no Doll would ever want to go through that! So you can understand why I wanna slack off, right?"
—Havoc's job interview

Doll skeleton destructive test complete. Test subject: damaged SI-DT series Doll. Test executor: SI-DT Havoc.
—SI-DT Final Test Record

Havoc's memorably laid-back personality has many causes. As recorded earlier, the long-term harsh and high-intensity working environment had a profound effect on her, but part of it really is just her nature—or perhaps a "shared" nature found widely in both humans and Dolls.

In most cases, Havoc won't spend even one extra second on work. She clocks in on time, clocks out on time, slacks off whenever she can, and never stays longer than she has to. When work is relatively slow, she'll even try every trick to skip out—until Arcadia upgraded to a more advanced recognition system and caught her red-handed. Still, if she's promised two or even three times the days off later, she doesn't mind putting more of her personal time into work. At the same time, she often bluntly criticizes workaholic behavior that sacrifices personal time.

"Three straight weeks of overtime? Sure, then I get three weeks off afterward!"
Even at the Oasis, she sticks firmly to this rule.

The SI-DT model is known for its staggeringly high attrition rate. Havoc herself has undergone many large-scale repairs, with almost every part except her mind core and head replaced at least once. She has also received multiple enhancements by "upgrading instead of repairing," such as swapping her arms' hydraulic systems for newer models so she can easily operate certain heavy machinery.

When the Neural Cloud project launched, Havoc was the SI-DT in the best overall condition, which is why Svarog and 42Lab picked her—and she herself was relatively positive about it, since it might let her escape her dangerous, suffocating work environment. She knew full well that if things went on like this, she'd someday end up like the SI-DTs retired or scrapped due to severe structural degradation.

Yet even though Havoc is good at regulating her own mind, her condition when she joined the Neural Cloud project wasn't great. Multiple mind modules were throwing over 10,000 errors, and the maintenance staff considered it a miracle that she was functioning at all. During the Wipe-off Incident, Havoc's already near-limit mind collapsed under outside influence, and every module lost connection. Fortunately, she was found by the Guardians and received proper treatment.

"Back then, even Havvie's language module was broken... but she still stuck with rehab alongside us. Now she's hardly any different from most Dolls!"
—De Lacey

Although she doesn't have to shoulder the Guardians' main field duties like the "Echo" squad, Havoc's tremendous strength and unusually high durability mean she's often sent on fairly high-risk field missions, usually mid- to high-intensity frontal combat. In such cases, Havoc typically demands more vacation as payment, and their boss usually doesn't refuse. However loose and lazy she looks, Havoc always gets the job done reliably, sometimes even brilliantly. She just occasionally needs a reminder not to overdo it.

"Havvie's terrifying strength... even that toy designer at the Oasis with her own unusual strength has to give her some respect."
—De Lacey

"Standing in front of her, you always feel... pressure... Though that feeling goes away fast once you see her not-so-bright face."
—Lind

"Triple pay and triple vacation is fine, of course. But if you go too far and cause extra trouble, I'll deduct triple, alright?"
—Sangoma, assigning missions on the eve of the decisive battle for Magrasea
oathDesc: Provider of adequate personal protection, in several senses.

Attire produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea. These are the clothes they are most comfortable in.
"Leave the protecting business to me. Just remember to leave enough time to slack off later, alright?"

projections.desc:
Attire and environment produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea, which mirrors their life in the real world.
"Ah—yawn. It's so warm and comfy, can't help but get sleepy... relax, the work's already been completed to perfection. As payment, how about being my body pillow for a bit?"
